extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent attorneys, agents and practitioners before the European Patent Office; national industrial property offices of Contracting States
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural, formal and substantive standards and requirements governing filing, prosecution, opposition, appeal and other proceedings for European patent applications and patents under the European Patent Convention (EPC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer and constitution of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent application may be transferred or give rise to rights for one or more of the designated Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment of a European patent application shall be made in writing and shall require the signature of the parties to the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent application may be licensed in whole or in part for the whole or part of the territories of the designated Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable law for application as property
rubrics_metrics.description: The European patent application as an object of property shall, in each designated Contracting State and with effect for such State, be subject to the law applicable in that State to national patent applications, unless otherwise specified in the Convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Places where application may be filed
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent application may be filed at the European Patent Office at Munich or its branch at The Hague, or, if permitted by national law, at the central industrial property office or other competent authority of a Contracting State; an application filed at a national authority shall have the same effect as if filed the same date at the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National laws may govern inventions not communicable abroad or may require initial national filing; filings at national offices are subject to such national provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on divisional filing at national offices
rubrics_metrics.description: No Contracting State may provide for or allow the filing of European divisional applications with an authority referred to for national filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: European divisional application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A European divisional application must be filed directly with the EPO; it may be filed only in respect of subject-matter which does not extend beyond the content of the earlier application as filed; if complied with the divisional is deemed filed on the earlier filing date and has benefit of priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional shall not designate Contracting States not designated in the earlier application; procedure, special conditions and time limits for fees are in Implementing Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding by national offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Central industrial property offices must forward European patent applications filed with them to the EPO in the shortest time compatible with national secrecy laws; applications obviously not subject to secrecy shall be forwarded within six weeks; those requiring further secrecy examination within four months (or 14 months if priority claimed); secret applications shall not be forwarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications not reaching the EPO before the end of the fourteenth month after filing (or after priority date if claimed) are deemed withdrawn and fees refunded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory contents of the European patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent application shall contain: (a) a request for the grant of a European patent; (b) a description of the invention; (c) one or more claims; (d) any drawings referred to in the description or claims; (e) an abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of filing and search fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent application shall be subject to the payment of the filing fee and the search fee within one month after the filing of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must also satisfy conditions in the Implementing Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Contracting States and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must contain designation of the Contracting State(s) in which protection is desired; designation is subject to payment of designation fee within 12 months after filing or priority date; designation may be withdrawn up to grant; withdrawal of all designations equals withdrawal of the application; designation fees shall not be refunded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of filing is the date on which documents filed contain: (a) an indication that a European patent is sought; (b) designation of at least one Contracting State; (c) information identifying the applicant; (d) a description and one or more claims in one of the official languages, even if other requirements are not complied with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of the inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: The European patent application shall designate the inventor. If the applicant is not the inventor or not the sole inventor, the designation shall contain a statement indicating the origin of the right to the European patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The European patent application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The European patent application must disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims shall define the matter for which protection is sought; they shall be clear and concise and be supported by the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and limits of the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall merely serve for use as technical information; it may not be taken into account for any other purpose, in particular not for interpreting the scope of protection sought nor for applying Article 54(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal fees for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal fees shall be paid to the EPO in respect of the third year and each subsequent year from the date of filing; late payment allowed within six months with additional fee; failure to pay leads to deemed withdrawal; obligation to pay ceases once renewal fee for year of publication of grant is paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who has duly filed an earlier patent/utility model etc. in a Paris Convention State (or equivalent filing) shall enjoy a right of priority for 12 months for filing a European application in respect of the same invention; equivalent regular national filings are recognised; rules concerning subsequent filings and non-Paris Convention States are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming priority formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim priority the applicant must file a declaration of priority, a copy of the previous application and, if its language is not one of the EPO official languages, a translation in an official language; procedure in Implementing Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple priorities permitted; priority covers only elements included in earlier application(s); elements not present among earlier claims can still be covered if the earlier application documents as a whole specifically disclose them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of priority shall count as the date of filing of the European patent application for the purposes of novelty/priority-related provisions (Article 54 and Article 60 references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination on filing (receiving section checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Receiving Section shall examine whether the application satisfies requirements for a date of filing, whether filing and search fees have been paid in due time, and whether required translations (where applicable) have been filed in due time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If date of filing cannot be accorded, the applicant may be given opportunity to correct deficiencies under Implementing Regulations; failure to remedy deficiencies results in the application not being dealt with as a European patent application; unpaid fees or missing translations lead to deemed withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a date of filing is accorded, the Receiving Section examines compliance with specified formal/physical requirements, that the abstract is filed, that the request satisfies mandatory Implementing Regulations provisions (including priority requirements), that designation fees are paid, that inventor designation is made, and that drawings referred to were filed on the date of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficiencies may be corrected according to Implementing Regulations; uncorrected deficiencies can lead to refusal and loss of priority; omission of inventor not corrected within 16 months (or priority date) can cause deemed withdrawal; missing drawings may lead to re-dating or deletion of references.

rubrics_metrics.name: European search report
rubrics_metrics.description: If a date of filing is accorded the Search Division shall draw up the European search report on the basis of the claims, with due regard to the description and any drawings, in the form prescribed in the Implementing Regulations and transmit it to the applicant with copies of cited documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of the application
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent application shall be published as soon as possible after 18 months from filing or from the priority date if claimed; applicant may request earlier publication; publication shall contain the description, claims, drawings and, in an annex, the search report and abstract if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If search report and abstract are not available at the time, they shall be published separately when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for examination and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for examination must be filed in writing up to the end of six months after the date on which the European Patent Bulletin mentions publication of the search report; the request is not filed until the examination fee is paid and may not be withdrawn; failure to file leads to deemed withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of period for examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Council may extend the period within which examination requests may be filed if applications cannot be examined in due time; it may decide third parties may be entitled to make requests and shall determine Implementing Regulations rules; decisions apply only to applications filed after publication of that decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If extended, measures must be laid down to restore original period as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If examination reveals the application or invention does not meet Convention requirements, the Examining Division shall invite the applicant (as often as necessary) to file observations within a fixed period; if applicant fails to reply in due time, the application shall be deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If request for examination was filed before search report transmission, EPO will invite the applicant after transmission to indicate whether to proceed further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal and grant conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examining Division shall refuse if application/invention does not meet requirements; shall decide to grant if they meet requirements provided: (a) applicant approves the text in which it intends to grant; (b) fees for grant and printing are paid within the time limit; (c) renewal and additional fees already due have been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fees not paid in due time the application is deemed withdrawn; decision to grant takes effect only when the Bulletin mentions the grant; translations of claims into the two other official languages may be required under Implementing Regulations, with time limits and failure to file leading to withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of granted patent specification
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time the mention of grant is published, the EPO shall publish a specification of the European patent containing the description, claims and any drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition timing and formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Within nine months from the publication of the mention of grant any person may file opposition to the European patent by giving notice to the EPO in a written reasoned statement; opposition is not filed until the opposition fee has been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition applies to the patent in all Contracting States in which it has effect; may be filed even if patent surrendered or lapsed; opponents and proprietor are parties to proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition may only be filed on grounds that: (a) the subject-matter of the patent is not patentable within Articles 52 to 57; (b) the patent does not disclose the invention sufficiently clearly and completely for a skilled person to carry it out; (c) the subject-matter extends beyond the content of the application as filed (or beyond the earlier application where patent granted on divisional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If admissible, the Opposition Division shall examine whether the grounds for opposition prejudice maintenance of the patent; in examination it shall invite parties, as often as necessary, to file observations within a period fixed by the Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination conducted in accordance with Implementing Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation, rejection or maintenance as amended
rubrics_metrics.description: The Opposition Division shall revoke the patent if grounds prejudice maintenance; reject the opposition if they do not; or decide to maintain the patent as amended provided the proprietor approves the text and the fee for printing a new specification is paid within the time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay printing fee leads to revocation; translations of amended claims into the two other official languages may be required and failure to file leads to revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of amended specification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a European patent is amended under maintenance, the EPO shall publish a new specification containing the amended description, claims and any drawings simultaneously with the mention of the opposition decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment and fixing of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party shall meet the costs he has incurred unless an Opposition Division or Board of Appeal orders a different apportionment for reasons of equity; the registry shall fix amounts on request and such fixing may be reviewed; final decisions fixing costs are enforceable like civil court decisions, limited to authenticity review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention by assumed infringer
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party who proves that infringement proceedings for the same patent have been instituted against him may, after the opposition period, intervene in opposition proceedings by filing a written reasoned notice within three months of institution; such intervention is treated as an opposition (subject to Implementing Regulations exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions subject to appeal and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal lies from decisions of the Receiving Section, Examining Divisions, Opposition Divisions and the Legal Division and shall have suspensive effect; an appeal may be filed against Opposition Division decisions even if the patent has been surrendered or lapsed; certain decisions (cost apportionment alone) cannot be sole subject of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may appeal and parties to appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party to proceedings adversely affected by a decision may appeal; any other parties to the proceedings shall be parties to the appeal proceedings as of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and form for appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of appeal must be filed in writing at the EPO within two months after notification of the decision; the notice is not filed until appeal fee is paid; within four months a written statement setting out the grounds of appeal must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory revision by first-instance department
rubrics_metrics.description: If the department whose decision is contested considers the appeal admissible and well founded it shall rectify its decision; if not allowed within one month after receipt of the statement of grounds it shall remit the appeal to the Board of Appeal without delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of appeals by Board of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appeal is admissible, the Board of Appeal shall examine whether the appeal is allowable and shall invite the parties, as often as necessary, to file observations within a fixed period; failure to reply in due time to invitation may lead to deemed withdrawal of the application (with specified exception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision powers and remittal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Appeal may exercise any power within the competence of the department whose decision was appealed or remit the case for further prosecution; departments remitted are bound by the ratio decidendi of the Board in so far as the facts are the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to the Enlarged Board of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board may refer questions of law to the Enlarged Board during proceedings if a decision is required to ensure uniform application of the law or if an important point of law arises; the President may refer where two Boards have given different decisions; parties to appeal proceedings are parties before the Enlarged Board; the Enlarged Board's decision is binding on the Board of Appeal in that case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of decisions (right to be heard / text limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of the EPO may only be based on grounds or evidence on which the parties concerned have had an opportunity to present their comments; the EPO shall consider and decide only in the text submitted to it, or agreed, by the applicant or proprietor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination by the EPO of its own motion
rubrics_metrics.description: In proceedings before it the EPO shall examine the facts of its own motion and shall not be restricted to facts, evidence and arguments provided by the parties; the EPO may disregard facts or evidence not submitted in due time by the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party observations after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Following publication of the application any person may present written observations concerning patentability, including a statement of grounds; such persons are not parties to proceedings but their observations shall be communicated to the applicant or proprietor who may comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral proceedings (when and publicity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral proceedings may take place at EPO instance if expedient or at request of any party; EPO may reject requests for further oral proceedings before the same department where parties and subject are the same; oral proceedings before Receiving/Examining/Legal Divisions shall not be public; proceedings (including decision delivery) before Boards of Appeal, Enlarged Board and, in so far as the department does not decide otherwise, before Opposition Divisions shall be public after publication of the application, unless public admission would cause serious and unjustified disadvantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means of taking evidence in proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In proceedings before an Examining Division, Opposition Division, Legal Division or Board of Appeal means of giving or obtaining evidence include: hearing the parties; requests for information; production of documents; hearing witnesses; opinions by experts; inspection; sworn statements in writing. The Examining/ Opposition Division or Board may commission a member to examine evidence.
